lessons.title: 1. If-Else Statements
lessons.description: C++ uses `if`, `else if`, and `else`. Implement `is_even(int n)` returning `true` if n is divisible by 2.
learning_objectives: Use if-else and % modulo operator in C++

lessons.title: 2. Logical Operators (&&, ||, !)
lessons.description: C++ uses `&&` for AND, `||` for OR, and `!` for NOT. Implement `can_drive(bool has_license, bool is_sober)`, which is true only when the driver holds a licence and is sober.
learning_objectives: Use logical AND && and OR || in C++

tests.name: test_can_drive
tests.test_code:
assert(can_drive(true, true) == true);
assert(can_drive(true, false) == false);

sublessons.title: Match the operator to its rule

exercises.question: Match each C++ expression to when it is true.

pairs.right: both a and b are true
at least one of a and b is true
n divides by 2 with no remainder

correct_answer.a && b: both a and b are true
correct_answer.a || b: at least one of a and b is true
correct_answer.n % 2 == 0: n divides by 2 with no remainder

exercises.explanation: `&&` needs both, `||` needs one, `!` flips, and `%` gives the remainder that decides divisibility.

lessons.title: 3. Temperature Alarm (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Return alarm status based on reactor core temperature.

lessons.title: 4. Triangle Validity (Practice)
lessons.description: Check if 3 side lengths can form a valid triangle.
learning_objectives: Apply triangle inequality theorem in C++

lessons.title: 5. Unit 2 Checkpoint: C++ Conditionals Mastery
lessons.description: Checkpoint for control flow: implement max_of_three(int a, int b, int c) returning the largest of the three values — nested if/else comparisons or std::max(a, std::max(b, c)). The test asserts max_of_three(10, 42, 25) == 42.
